name: Progressive Nodular Histiocytosis

criteria.description: Presence of multiple progressive cutaneous nodules with histiocytic infiltration
Skin biopsy showing dermal proliferation of spindle-shaped and foamy histiocytes without significant atypia
Immunohistochemical staining positive for CD68 and factor XIIIa, negative for CD1a and S100
Chronic progressive course with increasing number and size of nodules over months to years
No evidence of systemic organ involvement or malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple progressive cutaneous nodules with characteristic histopathology and immunohistochemistry findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other histiocytic disorders and systemic diseases.

laboratory: Absence of systemic inflammatory markers elevation
imaging: Ultrasound may show dermal thickening corresponding to nodules
other: Skin biopsy with characteristic histiocytic infiltration
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and factor XIIIa

distinguishingFeatures: Typically occurs in infants and young children
Lesions are usually solitary or few in number
Involves mucous membranes and systemic organs
Lesions are yellowish and more widespread

redFlags: Rapid increase in size or number of nodules
Ulceration or bleeding of skin lesions
Development of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
references: Fetsch JF, et al. Progressive nodular histiocytosis: a clinicopathologic study of 13 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 1997.
Weitzman S, Jaffe R. Histiocytic disorders of children and adults: introduction and overview. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2008.
